entities.name: FCGR1A
observations: CD64 expression in peripheral-blood leukocytes was higher in severe than mild acute pancreatitis and decreased during remission in a 2014 human cohort.
Flow-cytometric neutrophil CD64 was elevated in infected and septic acute pancreatitis and associated with severe disease, infected pancreatic necrosis, organ failure, and mortality risk.

entities.name: Acute pancreatitis
observations: Human studies consistently report increased CD64/nCD64 in severe or complicated acute pancreatitis. Findings include association with infected pancreatic necrosis, abdominal infection, sepsis, SIRS, ARDS, multiple-organ failure, and death.

entities.name: nCD64-IPN prediction
observations: In independent human training and validation cohorts, admission nCD64 was higher in infected pancreatic necrosis, with AUC 0.859 and 0.919; reported odds ratio was 2.971.
nCD64 should be considered an adjunctive biomarker because studies are observational and assay thresholds require external validation.

entities.name: nCD64-AP infection
observations: In a human cohort of 234 acute pancreatitis patients, CD64 index and CD64-positive rate were higher with abdominal infection and further increased with sepsis; CD64 index had 82.14% sensitivity and 88.51% specificity for infection.

entities.name: nCD64-AP mortality
observations: In a 302-patient human acute pancreatitis study, higher admission nCD64 was associated with SIRS, ARDS, multiple-organ failure, and death; a cutoff of 1.45 identified a group with no observed deaths in either cohort, with survival separation at p<0.001.
The available report did not provide endpoint-specific event counts, adjusted effect estimates, or AUCs.
